x: Blowfield did 4 mins. 27.6 secs., to finish in second place, and John Brown gained yet another third place medal. The 2 Miles Walk saw Harry Churcher beat Joe Coleman, the past holder, and D. McMullen finished third with Jack Rutland fourth.
Young McMullen, walking comfortably throughout, finished nearly a minute in front of Bert East, with Joe Wilson third. The handicap was won by Don Heath with Sid Spencer second and Joe Wilson third.

Dave McMullen was our next man showing good form early in the season, with evergreen East again among them and Pat Sapcote scoring in our first team over sevens, for the first time, thus showing he has speed as well as stamina.
At the end of the Common, Harry Churcher was well away in the lead followed by D. McMullen, Copperwheat, Miller and Tunbridge and it was evident that Churcher was going to cut out a very fast pace.

Unfortunately our hopes were dashed when we learnt that Dave McMullen who had walked splendidly up to then had been ruled out at 8½ miles. This shook our team men badly but Captain Charlie put in a grand effort and picked up places whilst our supporters got busy with their whips and flogged our team into life again.
Harry Churcher 1st and Dave McMullen 2nd in the London Business Houses Championship. Archie Bedford, who won the London Transport 5 miles Cross Country Championship.
…8 made last year, it was nevertheless a very sound performance. Harry Churcher won the 2 miles walk in easy fashion and D. McMullen finished second, as usual, one might say to Harry.…
The bright spot of the meeting was Harry Churcher's win in the 2 miles walk with D. McMullen third and we easily won the team race in conjunction.
I think McMullen, in the four miles, walked the best I have seen him do. The three and two miles were interesting races and the results remained in doubt until the last lap.

Derrick Burfitt was not defending his 1 mile Senior title and Jack Brown ran a good race to beat Len Herbert with Bob Taylor gaining his first club championship medal in third place. Dave McMullen retained his 2 miles walk title with A.
The support of Dave McMullen, Gerry Gregory and Syd James gave us second place and Harry Churcher and Dave McMullen gained second place medals for Surrey County in the Inter-County Championship.

It was true that we only had two individual title winners in the senior events and two in the junior, but the all-round performances of our members was very good, as you can see from the following results. In the 2 mile walk, although we filled first two places with Harry Churcher and Dave McMullen, the team race resulted in a tie between us and Cambridge Harriers.
Gregory won the two miles walk, with D.

At about half distance apart from Barrett of Cambridge Harriers, the front part of the race looked almost like a Belgrave Club race with Gerry Gregory, Harry Churcher, Dave McMullen and Syd James all on each other's heels.

With Harry Churcher 3rd and Dave McMullen 4th we had another scratch team win despite the fact that we lost George Checkley who was well up at about 3 miles and had to wait until 26th position was filled by Jack Rutland.

The absence of Dave McMullen and Gerry Gregory no doubt accounted for Surrey A.C.'s first scratch team win for many years, and with Paddy Woods narrowly beating Harry Churcher for individual honours, the Surrey boys are to be congratulated on their dual win.
It was good to see Dave McMullen back in circulation once again so soon after his return from the wild open spaces of Canada. We are expecting to see a lot more of you Mac.
Eric Hall still showing his good form, finished in the grand time of 1hr. 38m. 48secs. and Dave McMullen surprised us with a second placing in 1h. 39m. 28secs.

Our friendly rivals, Surrey W.C. were after our blood and when we lost Dave McMullen things were not so well. Eric Hall walked a very good race to win the individual title in 81m. 13secs. almost unchallenged and he was followed in 2nd place by Syd James, just over a minute behind.

In the three miles Dave McMullen 4th and Bob Newson 5th collected 45 points and we had a lead of 4 points. In the final race of 2 miles, Ted Smith was 2nd and Joe Coleman 6th making a grand total of 173 points and maintaining our lead of 4 points to win.
Stan Vickers was first home in 14m. 47.6 secs. with Eric Hall 2nd and Dave McMullen 3rd, followed by three more of our walkers and scoring 14 a side, we won the match by 144 points to 262.
With Dave McMullen 9th we easily won the team race with 10 points. Other positions were Ted Smith 10th, Ray Switzer 18th, Harry Shields 21st Bob Readman 22nd, D.

Our return match with Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec was held on 14th August when a field of 41 turned out. We provided the first five men home with Eric Hall, Dave McMullen, Ted Smith, Ray Switzer and G.
On 3rd July Ted Smith won the Business Houses 2 miles Track Walking Championship. D, McMullen was 3rd and M.

Our lads showed steady improvement and we were glad to see Dave McMullen and Syd James to the fore. Ted Smith was our first man home in (10th) followed by McMullen, Checkley and Newson, 12th, 15th and 16th.

Eric Hall retained his title, winning by 34 sec. from 2nd claim member George Williams who had travelled up from Worcester (that's enthusiasm). In the champioship Dave McMullen was 2nd and Syd James 3rd. Dave just pipped Williams for the handicap with Bob Readman a popular 3rd.

Eric broke away after half-a-mile and thereafter was in no danger of defeat. 63 sec. up at the half distance, he won by 2 min.15sec. from George, who had walked well and always held second place from Dave McMullen who suffered from cramp at 7 miles, but held 3rd place, finishing almost 2 min. ahead of the fourth man.
Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th!
We were without Syd James, and Dave McMullen was not at his best, owing to an attack of flu. First-class dressing accommodation was provided at a boy's school on the outskirts of Coventry.

A splendid race was won in immaculate style by Eric Hall who was just over one minute ahead of Dave McMullen.Then followed three other Belgravians which meant that the team race was won with the minimum score of ten points.
Dave McMullen walked a very even race indeed and was always in the first twenty. His 17th position at the finish was one of the soundest pieces of team work he has given us, and they have been many.

Dave McMullen, by finishing second, gave a good indication of his ability over this distance and a newcomer to the distance, J.Keown put up a sterling performance, and with a little more experience should soon be among the top notchers.

Veteran Dave McMullen was unable to travel and our team began to take on an attenuated appearance. However ten of our walkers plus General Goswell and others made the long journey to Leeds from whence coaches conveyed the party to Gomersal.
Second claim John Duckett slipped under the hour for the first time and evergreen Dave McMullen turned in a snappy 57.48 which made some of our younger members blush a bit.
In the same race Barry Ingarfield recorded a personal best 78:16 with Dave McMullen finishing 6th in 82:58. Joe and Percy Wilson brought up the rear in 104:24 and 105:52 respectively.

Barry Ingarfield and Dave McMullen both walked good races, prepared to shoulder the burden if necessary. Belgrave men were also prominent in the county race with Wilf and Carl featuring in Surrey's 2nd position and Alan Callow scoring for Lancashire who finished 3rd.
Without Callow, Lawton, Middleton and Coates it was left to Ingarfield to lead the team home backed up by Len Duquemin, John Dunsford and sprightly Dave McMullen.
With Ray Middleton and Allan Callow backing up, Bels took the team and there was also some good walking by the Johns Dunsford and Hall, who came in together with Dave McMullen not far behind.
Belgrave were 2nd team to Southend with Lawton, Ray Middleton and John Hall in the Bels. team. Our other walkers were John Dunsford, Dave McMullen, John Bromley and Ray Hall.

The eventual winner was Ken Harding (40 to 50 age group) with a doubtful Joe Barraclough (two warnings and international rules applying)* 2nd and Len Duquemin 3rd. Dave McMullen won the 50 to 60 age group. * See the Pryor report on Race Walking, pub. by I.A.A.F. 72.

Dave McMullen was first Veteran, John Bromley picked up fourth handicap and Bob Carter one of the raffle prizes. In fact it was an all round performance with our team of eight all in the first 41 places.

John Dunsford had his days as did Dave McMullen, in between his complaints about his performances, despite his gold G.L.C. medal. Ray Hall began to regain his fitness but a stomach virus put paid to that.
He was almost caught by Dave McMullen and Ray Hall. Bob Picton it seems is getting less fat and more fit, maybe he is aiming to do well in the 'Garnet'.
Dave "I'll never break the hour again" McMullen only had 2 minutes 44 seconds to spare and Len Evans, Martin Bennett and John Dunsford also were under the hour.
Ray Middleton came in 10th followed by John Hall with Dave McMullen (dare we say a sprightly 52) being 4th man to bring home the team to a comfortable win.
John Hall walked a rather sleepy sort of race and never got going but John Dunsford delighted in turning the tables on Dave McMullen again. Ray Hall, not too fit at the moment,was our 8th man.
Dave McMullen and Ray Hall walked their way back into the county team and Eric Stroud turned in a commendable performance on the tough course.
Time and again it is proved that advancing years are no excuse for a falling off in ability. Our evergreen walker DAVE McMULLEN was recently selected to represent Surrey at the age of 53.
Further back, John Hall walked quite a good one in the hot conditions to beat Southend's Banyard and Rosser whilst Dave McMullen came under the judges ban as did many other men.

He welcomes any other Belgrave members to visit him and stay, and always has plenty of food in, although not much space to eat it in as so much room is taken up by the freezer. Our junior members, Dave McMullen, Ray Middleton, etc., will wonder just who Cameron is or has been.

Although we scratched a team together to start this race (Dave McMullen went to the wrong venue) we failed to finish one due to Carl Lawton's retirement at 13 miles, leaving Ray Hall to be our first man home in 9th position.
John Hall placed 31st with John Dunsford and Dave McMullen well up. Ray Hall was forced to retire but Bob Picton and John Keown completed the distance.
The tenacity of Dave McMullen, D.Hall and John Dunsford showed this spirit and the pity was that E.Stroud could not be included in the team and rewarded for his fine walk.
In the Surrey Championship we once again secured double honours, Harry Churcher leading the team in his usual style, followed by Charlie, Mac (Dave McMullen) and Bert East.
The forward walking of John Hall must give him great satisfaction while Dave McMullen, who took part in the first Championship, can only be described as a phenomenon.

John Bromley gave us 2nd team in the Leicester Mercury, Dave McMullen, 2nd team Lambeth, and Bob Farley, winning team Hastings to Brighton. We pulled up well to be 2nd team in the National 50km after a bad one in the '20'.
In the Vets AC Championship held at Battersea Park on July 7th over 3,200 metres, Dave McMullen came home 2nd in 15:30 behind K.Livermore (Woodford Green).15:09.

Laurie O'Hara took the 1,500 metres in 4:13.6 and the 5,000 metres in 15:14.0, and Clive Shippen won the 3,000 metre steeplechase with 10:12.4. In the 50 - 54 age group Dave McMullen stepped it out to a 14:40.2 3,000 metre walk victory.
That well known veteran walker DAVE McMULLEN tells us that his father BOB McMULLEN, now over 80, is still active and well and enjoys a game of golf at Mitcham.
Three of our walkers are hoping to go to Toronto, Canada in August to compete in some veteran events, so good luck to DAVE McMULLEN, JOHN BROMLEY and JOHN DUNSFORD.
After a great effort Dave McMullen finished twelfth to give S.W.C. and ourselves 20 points each, Surrey gaining the day by the higher placing of their fourth man.
Meanwhile over at Luton our reserves were sweeping up in the Open 10km by taking first team place as well as fourth scorer Dave McMullen taking the Vets award.
They were 6th Dave McMullen with 26:03, 9th Doug. Fotheringham with 26:30, 10th John Hall with 26:42, 13th Martin Bennett with 28:21 and 18th Joe Scamell with 30:14.
In the 25 kilometre walk at the World Masters Championships in Vancouver John Dunsford finished 6th in the 40 - 44 age group in 2:13:50 whilst Dave McMullen in the 50 - 54 group was 4th in 2:27:00
Fotheringham and Dave McMullen coming through for third team overall. Nigel Morris as mentioned earlier was involved in an accident early in December when he succeeded in breaking a leg and an arm.

Doug Fotheringham got to the finish nine seconds ahead of Dave McMullen with "Bomber" Bromley backing up. Towards the front it was only in the closing stages that Carl Lawton pushed into second slot, overtaking Seddon (BoE) and holding Greasley (Sheffield) at bay by four seconds.

We had plenty of non-scoring backing including our three remarkable veterans Dave McMullen, John Dunsford and Doug Fotheringham. Our Newham AC member, Mike Scamell, continues to improve, as shown by his consistant high placings.

Other Belgravians at the Southern Vets were Dave McMullen, who was first in the 2B 3,000 metres Walk with 15:08.0, and Charlie Speechley who placed second in the 5B 100 metres - 0.5 behind the 'Tartan Flash' Duncan McLean.
